parts.title: Why do we keep pets?
paras: Around half of all households in Britain are (0) home to at least one pet. Dogs and cats are the most popular, but rabbits, fish and even snakes have their [[1]] of fans. Scientists have long tried to understand why we [[2]] so much time and money on animals that give us nothing practical in return.

One answer is that pets are good for our health. Studies have shown that stroking a dog can [[3]] blood pressure, and dog owners tend to take more exercise than other people. For people who live alone, a pet can also be a great [[4]] of comfort.

However, owning a pet is a big [[5]]. Dogs need walking [[6]] of the weather, and many animals live for well over a decade. Animal charities [[7]] people to think carefully before buying a pet, as thousands are abandoned every year when their owners lose [[8]] in them.

q.expl: Устойчивое have their share of — тоже иметь (своих поклонников, проблем и т. п.).
spend time and money on sth — тратить время и деньги на что-то. Pass time — коротать время, pay требует for, put — into.
Нужен переходный глагол: lower blood pressure — понизить давление. Fall, sink, decline не берут дополнения.
a source of comfort — источник утешения.
a big commitment — серьёзное обязательство, требующее времени и сил. Engagement — помолвка или встреча, attachment — привязанность.
regardless of — независимо от. Despite идёт без of, although — с предложением, however — наречие.
urge sb to do sth — настоятельно призывать. Insist требует on или that, demand и suggest не используются с sb to do.
lose interest in sth — потерять интерес к чему-то.

parts.name: Open cloze
parts.instr: For questions 9–16, read the text below and think of the word which best fits each gap. Use only one word in each gap. There is an example at the beginning (0).
parts.title: A hotel made of ice
paras: Every winter, in the far north of Sweden, a hotel is built entirely (0) out of ice and snow. Artists from all over the world are invited to design the rooms, [[9]] means that no two are ever the same.

Guests sleep on beds made of ice, covered [[10]] reindeer skins, and are given thick sleeping bags to keep them warm. The temperature inside the rooms stays at around minus five degrees, [[11]] matter how cold it is outside.

Spending a night there is not for everyone. Most guests stay [[12]] one night only and then move to a warm room in the main building. Even so, [[13]] of them say it is one of the most memorable experiences of their lives.

In spring, the hotel slowly melts, and the water flows back into the river [[14]] which the ice was taken. Work on the next hotel begins [[15]] soon as winter returns, and the whole process starts all [[16]] again.

q.expl: После запятой which относится ко всей предыдущей мысли: художники каждый год разные — и это значит, что…
covered with (или in) reindeer skins — покрытые оленьими шкурами.
no matter how — как бы ни.
stay for one night — остаться на одну ночь.
many (или most) of them — многие (большинство) из них.
Предлог переходит в начало придаточного: the river from which the ice was taken = the river the ice was taken from.
as soon as — как только.
start all over again — начать всё заново.

Being an influencer looks easy, but it can be surprisingly [[19]]. Successful influencers post content almost every day and must constantly deal with [[20]] from strangers. Some admit that the pressure to appear [[21]] all the time has made them deeply [[22]].
In many countries, influencers are now required to state [[23]] when a post has been paid for, so that their followers are not [[24]].

q.expl: После their нужно существительное, и по смыслу во множественном числе (who often trust): followers.
Перед adverts нужно прилагательное: traditional.
demanding — требующий много сил, тяжёлый.

По смыслу (давление вредит) — unhappy, с отрицательной приставкой.
К глаголу state нужно наречие: clearly.

parts.name: Multiple choice
parts.instr: You are going to read an article about a teenager who records the weather. For questions 31–36, choose the answer (A, B, C or D) which you think fits best according to the text.
parts.title: The weather watcher
parts.subtitle: Fourteen-year-old Isla Brennan has been recording the weather every day for five years. Now scientists use her data.
paras: Isla Brennan was nine when she started writing down the weather. Every morning before school, she would check the thermometer outside the kitchen window and note the temperature in a school exercise book, along with a few words about the sky. 'I don't really know why I started,' she says. 'I think I just liked having something that was completely mine.' Five years and twenty-three exercise books later, the habit has turned into something rather more serious.

For her twelfth birthday, her grandparents gave her a proper weather station, which now stands in the back garden. It measures rainfall, wind speed and humidity, and sends the readings to her laptop every ten minutes. Isla checks them obsessively. 'My friends tease me about it,' she admits. 'If we're out somewhere and it starts raining, they all turn to me as if I'm personally responsible.'

Last year, she discovered that the national weather service accepts data from volunteer observers, as long as their equipment meets certain standards. Getting approved took months. An inspector visited to check that the station was the correct height and far enough from walls and trees, and asked Isla a long list of questions. 'I was terrified,' she laughs. 'But at the end he said my records were tidier than some of the professional ones he'd seen.'

Her readings are now added to a national database that scientists use to study long-term changes in the climate. Isla finds this both exciting and slightly worrying. 'When I look back through my old exercise books, I can already see that our winters are getting milder,' she says. 'It's only five years, so it doesn't prove anything on its own. But it makes the news feel a lot less abstract.'

Isla wants to study meteorology at university, but she has no intention of giving up her own station. 'Professional forecasters work with huge computer models,' she says. 'I love that, but there's something about going outside every morning and looking at the sky for yourself. A computer can't tell you what the air smells like before a storm.'

q.stem: Why did Isla first start recording the weather?
opts: Her teacher had given her a project.
She liked having something of her own.
She was worried about climate change.
Her parents encouraged her to do it.
q.hl: I think I just liked having something that was completely mine.
q.expl: Она не знает точно почему, но ей нравилось иметь что-то только своё. Школьная тетрадь — просто тетрадь, а не задание (A).

q.stem: What does Isla say about her friends?
opts: They are not interested in the weather.
They make fun of her hobby.
They often ask her for forecasts.
They genuinely blame her when it rains.
q.hl: My friends tease me about it
q.expl: Друзья подшучивают над ней. Ловушка D: «as if I'm personally responsible» — это шутка, а не настоящие обвинения.

q.stem: How did Isla feel about the inspector's visit?
opts: She was confident that it would go well.
She was scared at the time but pleased with the outcome.
She thought some of his questions were unfair.
She was disappointed by his comments.
q.hl: my records were tidier than some of the professional ones
q.expl: «I was terrified» — было страшно, но в конце инспектор сказал, что её записи аккуратнее профессиональных.

q.stem: What does Isla say about the changes she has noticed in her records?
opts: They prove that the climate is changing.
They are too small to be noticed.
They make climate change feel more real to her.
They have surprised the scientists she works with.
q.hl: it makes the news feel a lot less abstract
q.expl: Новости о климате становятся для неё менее абстрактными. Ловушка A: она прямо говорит, что пять лет сами по себе ничего не доказывают.

q.stem: What does 'it' refer to in 'it doesn't prove anything on its own'?
q.hl: It's only five years, so it doesn't prove anything on its own.
q.expl: «It's only five years» — речь о её пятилетних записях: сами по себе они ничего не доказывают.

q.stem: What does Isla's final comment suggest?
opts: She doubts that computer models are accurate.
She values observing the weather for herself.
She would prefer not to work as a forecaster.
She plans to design her own forecasting system.
q.hl: A computer can't tell you what the air smells like before a storm.
q.expl: Ей важно самой выходить и смотреть на небо — компьютер не расскажет, как пахнет воздух перед грозой. Модели она любит (A неверно) и хочет стать метеорологом (C неверно).

parts.name: Gapped text
parts.instr: You are going to read an article about a family who swapped homes for a month. Six sentences have been removed from the article. Choose from the sentences A–G the one which fits each gap (37–42). There is one extra sentence which you do not need to use.
parts.title: Our house is your house
parts.subtitle: Last summer, the Kowalski family swapped homes with a family in Portugal for a month. Anna Kowalski describes the experience.
paras: The idea came from my sister, who had been swapping homes for years. I was doubtful. [[37]] She just laughed and said that, in all her years of swapping, nothing had ever gone missing.
We joined a home-exchange website and created a profile with photos of our flat and the neighbourhood. [[38]] Within a week, we had received offers from families in Spain, Canada and Portugal.
We chose a family from Porto, partly because their house had a garden and partly because they also had two children. [[39]] By the time we exchanged keys, I felt as if I knew them.

Living in someone else's home turned out to be very different from staying in a hotel. [[40]] The children played with toys that weren't theirs, and we shopped at the local market like everyone else on the street.

Of course, there were small problems. The washing machine broke down in the second week, and we spent a whole morning trying to explain the problem to a repairman who spoke no English. [[41]] Our hosts, meanwhile, had to deal with our unreliable boiler back home.
Would we do it again? Without hesitation. [[42]] What we gained instead was a glimpse of what it is really like to live somewhere else – and two new friends in Porto.

sents.A: Wouldn't it be strange, I asked, to have strangers sleeping in our beds and looking through our cupboards?
sents.B: To my surprise, the response was immediate.
sents.C: We spent weeks emailing and even had a couple of video calls.
sents.D: We cooked in their kitchen, read their books and sat in their garden every evening.
sents.E: In the end, a neighbour came round and translated for us.
sents.F: We saved a lot of money on accommodation, but money was never really the point.
sents.G: Some of our friends still think we were mad to try it.

q.expl: «I was doubtful» → в чём сомнение: не странно ли пускать чужих в свои кровати и шкафы? (A) → «She just laughed and said… nothing had ever gone missing» — ответ на этот вопрос.
Создали профиль → к удивлению, отклик был мгновенным (B) → за неделю пришли предложения из трёх стран.
Выбрали семью из Порту → неделями переписывались и созванивались (C) → к обмену ключами казалось, что знает их.
Не как в отеле → готовили на их кухне, читали их книги (D) → дети играли с чужими игрушками. Перечисление продолжается.
Мастер не говорил по-английски → в итоге пришёл сосед и перевёл (E).
Сэкономили, но дело было не в деньгах (F) → «What we gained instead was…» — instead противопоставляет деньгам настоящую ценность. Ловушка G: про друзей не связывается со словом instead.

parts.name: Multiple matching
parts.instr: You are going to read an article about four festivals. For questions 43–52, choose from the festivals (A–D). The festivals may be chosen more than once.
parts.title: Four festivals worth the trip

texts.name: Lantern Night
texts.body: Every October, thousands of paper lanterns are released onto the river that runs through the old town, turning the water into a moving ribbon of light. Anyone can make a lantern at the free workshops held in the library the week before. The event itself costs nothing to attend, but be warned: the bridges get extremely crowded, and if you want a good view, you'll need to arrive at least two hours early. Afterwards, many of the cafés along the river stay open until midnight.

texts.name: The Mountain Film Festival
texts.body: Held in a huge heated tent at the foot of the ski slopes, this five-day festival shows films about climbing, sailing and other outdoor adventures. Many of the film-makers attend in person and answer questions after the screenings. Tickets go on sale in June and usually sell out within days, so set a reminder. If you miss out, the best films are shown again online a month later – though watching on a laptop isn't quite the same as hearing an audience gasp.

texts.name: The Street Food Weekend
texts.body: More than eighty stalls fill the old bus station for this weekend celebration of food from around the world. Prices are reasonable, and there's an impressive choice of vegetarian dishes. Bring a card rather than cash: none of the stalls accept notes or coins. With face painting, a climbing wall and a quiet area for babies, it's ideal for families. The only drawback is the lack of seating, so you may end up eating standing up.

texts.name: The Silent Disco Festival
texts.body: Picture a field full of people dancing in complete silence – until you put on the headphones. Each pair has three channels, and you can switch between DJs whenever you like, so you never have to agree on the music with your friends. The festival is strictly for over-sixteens, and ID is checked at the gate. Headphones are included in the ticket price, but you have to leave a deposit, which you get back when you return them at the end of the night.

q.stem: can still be enjoyed at home if you do not get a ticket?
q.hl: the best films are shown again online a month later
q.expl: Лучшие фильмы через месяц показывают онлайн.

q.stem: requires visitors to prove their age?
q.hl: ID is checked at the gate
q.expl: Строго 16+, документы проверяют на входе.

q.stem: offers free sessions to help you take part?

q.expl: Фонарик можно сделать на бесплатных мастер-классах в библиотеке.

q.stem: accepts only one method of payment?
q.hl: none of the stalls accept notes or coins
q.expl: Наличные не принимают — только карта.

q.stem: gives visitors the chance to meet the people who created what they are watching?
q.hl: Many of the film-makers attend in person
q.expl: Режиссёры приезжают и отвечают на вопросы после показов.

q.stem: is particularly suitable for people with young children?
q.expl: Аквагрим, скалодром, тихая зона для малышей — идеально для семей.

q.stem: asks visitors to pay an amount that they will get back later?
q.hl: you have to leave a deposit
q.expl: За наушники берут залог и возвращают его в конце вечера.

q.stem: recommends arriving well before the event begins?
q.hl: you'll need to arrive at least two hours early
q.expl: Чтобы хорошо видеть, приходить минимум за два часа. Ловушка B: там советуют заранее купить билеты, а не прийти пораньше.

q.stem: lets visitors choose their entertainment without agreeing with their friends?
q.hl: you never have to agree on the music with your friends
q.expl: Три канала с разными диджеями — каждый слушает своё.

q.hl: The only drawback is the lack of seating
q.expl: Не хватает мест, чтобы сесть, — приходится есть стоя.
